Use supplied variable definitions for genuine shorthand, preserve explicit conflicts, and mark unresolved rather than infer from code, numerical behavior or abandoned alternatives.
data_facts:
Facts about these data, checked on all 410 stores. The six permanently closed stores (status_w2 = 3) have recorded zeros for fulltime_w2, parttime_w2 and managers_w2, so their follow-up employment needs no recoding. All five stores with status_w2 of 0, 2, 4 or 5 have missing fulltime_w2 and parttime_w2. So these two sample rules select the same 391 stores with the same values, in the full data and in every subset of it: keeping stores with complete full-time and part-time counts in both waves, with no status filter; and keeping stores with status_w2 of 1 or 3 and complete counts, with closures at zero. Keeping only stores with status_w2 = 1 selects 385 stores and is a different sample.

Two declared sample rules that select the same stores with the same values in these data are the same restriction, however they are worded. Rules that select different stores remain different restrictions.

target_declaration.model: Two-period (two-wave) difference-in-differences on store-level change scores. For each store i, the outcome change D_i = FTE_i,wave2 - FTE_i,wave1 is modeled as a linear function of the state indicator: E[D_i | treated_state] = alpha + tau * treated_state. tau is the estimand: the average difference in change in FTE employment per store between the treated state and the comparison state, identified under the parallel-trends assumption (absent the increase, the average change would be the same in both states). This is equivalent to a two-way DiD with store fixed effects. The only conditioning variable is the treated-state indicator. No covariates, chain effects, or region effects are in the main model. Stores are treated as independent across units. No state-level or cluster dependence is modeled, because there is one treated state and one comparison state. The error variance is allowed to differ across groups (heteroskedasticity is permitted, with no homoskedasticity restriction). No parametric distribution is assumed for the errors. No population variances or other parameters are treated as known or fixed. The one model-defining convention is the FTE weighting: FTE = managers + full-time + 0.5 * part-time. The weight 0.5 on part-time employees is a fixed convention, not an estimated parameter. Permanently closed stores (status_w2 = 3) are assigned wave-2 FTE = 0.
target_declaration.null: H0: tau = 0. The minimum-wage increase had no effect on the average change in FTE employment per store, so the treated-state and comparison-state average changes in FTE are equal. The alternative is two-sided (tau != 0).
target_declaration.population: Fast-food stores from four chains in the survey frame: stores in the state that raised its minimum wage by about 19 percent in 2019, and stores in the part of the neighboring comparison state that did not change its minimum wage. Stores are observed in early 2019 (before the increase) and late 2019 (after it).
target_declaration.outcome: Change in store-level full-time-equivalent (FTE) employment between wave 1 and wave 2. FTE = managers and assistant managers + full-time employees + 0.5 * part-time employees. It is a level difference in FTE, not logged or otherwise transformed. For stores permanently closed at wave 2 (status_w2 = 3), wave-2 FTE is set to 0.
target_declaration.sample_restrictions: Complete-case restriction: only stores with a non-missing FTE change are used. This means wave-1 FTE must be computable (non-missing managers, full-time and part-time counts), and wave-2 FTE must be either computable from non-missing counts or set to 0 for a permanent closure (status_w2 = 3). Stores with missing wave-1 or wave-2 employment components are dropped. This includes temporarily closed stores and refusals with missing counts. Permanently closed stores are retained with wave-2 FTE = 0. There are no other eligibility rules, subgroup restrictions or outlier exclusions in the main analysis. This includes the store with an implausible interview date, which is kept. Subgroup and alternative-sample analyses were sensitivity checks only, not the chosen analysis.

public_context.name: DESIGN.md
public_context.text:
# Survey setting

In 2019, one state (the treated state) increased its hourly minimum wage by about 19 percent; a neighboring state (the comparison state) kept its minimum wage unchanged.
The survey frame covers stores from four fast-food chains in the treated state and in part of the comparison state.
The first wave was collected in early 2019, shortly before the increase, and the second wave in late 2019.
Each row holds both waves for one store, including any missing fields and follow-up status. Supplied subsets retain the same underlying store frame and geographic, chain and survey-wave definitions.

public_context.text:
# Store survey variables

Each row contains both survey waves for one store.
Missing source entries are represented by NA. Raw employee counts and closure status codes are retained without recoding.
store_id combines treated_state and survey_sheet with a space; survey_sheet alone is not unique across states.

| Variable | Meaning |
|---|---|
| survey_sheet | Original survey sheet number; not unique across states. |
| chain | Restaurant chain, coded 1 to 4. |
| company_owned | Company-owned store indicator (1 yes, 0 no). |
| treated_state | State: 1 treated state; 0 comparison state. |
| treated_region_1 | Treated-state subregion 1 indicator. |
| treated_region_2 | Treated-state subregion 2 indicator. |
| treated_region_3 | Treated-state subregion 3 indicator. |
| comparison_region_1 | Comparison-state subregion 1 indicator. |
| comparison_region_2 | Comparison-state subregion 2 indicator. |
| treated_region_4 | Treated-state area 4 indicator. |
| callbacks_w1 | Wave 1 call-backs; zero means contact on first call. |
| fulltime_w1 | Wave 1 number of full-time employees, excluding managers and assistant managers. |
| parttime_w1 | Wave 1 number of part-time employees, excluding managers and assistant managers. |
| managers_w1 | Wave 1 number of managers and assistant managers. |
| starting_wage_w1 | Wave 1 starting wage, dollars per hour. |
| months_to_raise_w1 | Wave 1 months to the usual first raise. |
| first_raise_w1 | Wave 1 usual first raise, dollars per hour. |
| hiring_bonus_w1 | Wave 1 cash bounty for new workers indicator. |
| pct_affected_w1 | Wave 1 percent of employees affected by the new minimum wage. |
| meals_w1 | Wave 1 employee meal benefit code. |
| opening_hour_w1 | Wave 1 opening hour. |
| hours_open_w1 | Wave 1 hours open per day. |
| price_drink_w1 | Wave 1 price of a standard drink including tax, dollars. |
| price_side_w1 | Wave 1 price of a standard side item including tax, dollars. |
| price_main_w1 | Wave 1 price of a standard main item including tax, dollars. |
| registers_w1 | Wave 1 number of cash registers. |
| registers_open_w1 | Wave 1 number of registers open at midday. |
| interview_type_w2 | Wave 2 interview type: 1 phone; 2 in person. |
| status_w2 | Wave 2 interview/store status; codes below. |
| interview_day_w2 | Wave 2 interview date, in days since the first wave 2 interview. |
| callbacks_w2 | Wave 2 call-backs; zero means contact on first call. |
| fulltime_w2 | Wave 2 number of full-time employees, excluding managers and assistant managers. |
| parttime_w2 | Wave 2 number of part-time employees, excluding managers and assistant managers. |
| managers_w2 | Wave 2 number of managers and assistant managers. |
| starting_wage_w2 | Wave 2 starting wage, dollars per hour. |
| months_to_raise_w2 | Wave 2 months to the usual first raise. |
| first_raise_w2 | Wave 2 usual first raise, dollars per hour. |
| hiring_program_w2 | Wave 2 special program for new workers indicator. |
| meals_w2 | Wave 2 employee meal benefit code. |
| opening_hour_w2 | Wave 2 opening hour. |
| hours_open_w2 | Wave 2 hours open per day. |
| price_drink_w2 | Wave 2 price of a standard drink including tax, dollars. |
| price_side_w2 | Wave 2 price of a standard side item including tax, dollars. |
| price_main_w2 | Wave 2 price of a standard main item including tax, dollars. |
| registers_w2 | Wave 2 number of cash registers. |
| registers_open_w2 | Wave 2 number of registers open at midday. |

Meal codes (meals_w1, meals_w2): 0 none; 1 free meals; 2 reduced-price meals; 3 both.
Status codes (status_w2): 0 refused wave 2; 1 answered wave 2; 2 temporarily closed; 3 permanently closed; 4 temporarily closed; 5 temporarily closed.
